newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: YUGOSLAVS OPTIMISTIC AHEAD OF QUALIFYER WITH CZECHS.
newsitem.headline: YUGOSLAVS OPTIMISTIC AHEAD OF QUALIFYER WITH CZECHS.

text.p: The Yugoslav national soccer team was optimistic on Friday ahead of a world soccer championship qualifier against the Czech national team here on Sunday.
"We are going to give it all we got and I believe there will be no problem. Chances are 98.5 against 1.5 percent in ourt favour," Slavisa Jokanovic, the team's midfield, told Belgrade newspaper Blic.
Yugoslavia and the Czech Republic meet on Sunday at the Red Star stadium, the Belgrade's largest, in a qualifying match for the world championship next year in France.
Tradition is against the Yugoslavs. National teams of former Yugoslavia and Czechoslovakia have played 31 times so far and the Czechoslovaks had won 18 times.
This is the first time the national teams of the two new countries meet.
"I am not afraid of anything or anyone," Yugoslav team manager Slobodan Santrac said.
"Over the past days we have worked on adjusting our game and viewing tapes of the Czechs play."
"Our team is exceptionally strong, as individuals and as a collective. So the Czechs have something to worry about," he said.
Santrac also said Dejan Savicevic, the centre of the Italian club Milan, will not play due to injuries sustained in the match against Pharoe Islands last month.
